data.title: Quebecor Defends Telus Bid, Criticizes Potential BCE Countermove
data.description:
By Adriano Marchese

Quebecor pushed back against a potential rival tie-up between BCE and Telus, saying that a merger of the two major telecoms would hurt Canadian consumers.

The statement follows a Globe and Mail report on Wednesday that BCE's Bell Canada had opened preliminary talks with Telus to evaluate its options in response to Quebecor's unsolicited takeover bid.

Earlier in the week, Quebecor proposed a combination with Telus worth 31.31 billion Canadian dollars ($21.85 billion),or about C$19.45 a share, representing a roughly 60% premium to Telus' closing share price on the Toronto Stock Exchange last Friday, according to Quebecor.

Quebecor said Thursday that while Canada's telecommunication sector needs greater scale to compete with U.S. technology and satellite players, only its proposal would protect competition and lower prices.

BCE wasn't immediately available for comment.

The company added that it looks forward to meeting with Telus management on Nov. 23.

Write to Adriano Marchese at adriano.marchese@wsj.com

data.title: Alam Energy, Zeroboard to support corp decarbonisation in Indonesia
data.description:
November 19 (Renewables Now) - PT Alam Energy Renewables intends to support the decarbonisation management of companies in Indonesia as part of a new partnership with Zeroboard Inc, a Japanese cloud service for the calculation, disclosure and reduction of greenhouse gas emissions.

The two companies have signed an agreement to combine emissions visualisation with the offerings of Alam Energy, including rooftop solar power and renewable energy certificates (I-REC), it was announced on Wednesday.

The duo will hold joint seminars and provide support from emissions calculation to reduction for local companies, contributing to the domestic government’s goal to reach net zero emissions by 2060.

Alam Energy is owned by Shizen Energy Inc, Alamport Inc, NiX Japan Group, EnBio Holdings Inc and Kanematsu Corporation. As of October 2026, the business operates 39.5 MWp of rooftop solar power systems spread across 31 sites in Indonesia, mainly for Japanese manufacturers.

data.title: ASTS Stock Gets A Breather After Relentless Sell-Off: B. Riley Says Launch Delays, Funding Risks Are Already Priced In
data.description:
Key points:
  • B. Riley upgraded the satellite communications company to ‘Buy’ from ‘Neutral,’ according to The Fly.
  • On Wednesday, William Blair reiterated its ‘Market Perform’ rating on ASTS after ULA’s preliminary findings eased BE-4 engine concerns.
  • AST SpaceMobile is expected to use Blue Origin’s rockets with BE-4 engines next year.

AST SpaceMobile (ASTS) received an upgrade from B. Riley, which raised its rating to ‘Buy’ from ‘Neutral’ on Wednesday, stating that the shares have already priced in concerns over the company’s capital commitment, satellite deployment delays, and its rocket development partnership with Firefly Aerospace (FLY).

ASTS stock was up about 8% at the time of writing and on track for a first gain in six sessions. It has declined more than 39% over the past one month as of Wednesday’s close.

B. Riley Sees 73% Upside Potential

According to The Fly, B. Riley maintained its $48 price target on ASTS, implying a 73% upside from current levels. However, it is still well short of the 12-month consensus estimate of $63.35, according to Koyfin.

The firm now sees a more attractive risk-reward balance and believes investors are overlooking the potential benefits of developing its own launch capabilities, as well as “other positive catalysts.”

FireFly Partnership In Spotlight

B. Riley’s comments on AST SpaceMobile developing its own launch capabilities follow the company's announcement that it plans to develop its reusable Blacklift rocket, using Firefly’s Miranda and Vira engines, targeting launches starting in late 2028. On Tuesday, AST issued 10 million shares to Firefly under the agreement.

The partnership aims to reduce AST’s dependence on external launch providers and give it greater control over satellite deployments.

ULA’s Initial Findings Ease Engine Concerns

On Wednesday, William Blair reiterated its ‘Market Perform’ rating on ASTS after United Launch Alliance (ULA) said that preliminary findings from its November 15 Vulcan rocket launch failure, which destroyed 40 Amazon Leo satellites, pointed to inadequate fuel supply rather than performance of the BE-4 engines. The BE-4 rocket engine is developed by Blue Origin.

The findings are crucial because AST SpaceMobile expects to launch three BlueBird satellites aboard Blue Origin’s New Glenn rocket in early 2027. New Glenn uses the same BE-4 engine model as Vulcan.

However, the investigation remains ongoing under Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) oversight, ULA said.

Retail Sees Long-Term Opportunity

Retail sentiment surrounding ASTS on Stocktwits remained ‘neutral’ over the past 24 hours, amid a 78% jump in message volumes.

One user believes ASTS is “going to be a great opportunity for long-term investors.”

View this Stocktwits post

ASTS shares have been under heavy selling pressure this year, tanking more than 61%.

data.title: Strong dollar, tighter Fed policy bets leave gold to languish at 14-month low
data.description:
Key points:
  • Bullion touched its lowest level since Sept 2025 in the session
  • Markets see 91% chance of a 25-bp rate hike next month
  • Recent computer outages, AI worries could lead investors to 'hard assets' like gold, analyst says

By Anjana Anil

Gold eased to a 14-month low on Thursday, as it continued to face pressure from strength in the US dollar, with markets fully pricing in a rate hike at the Federal Reserve's December meeting owing to stubborn inflation.

Spot gold was down 0.3% at $3,710.29 per ounce by 9:15 a.m. ET (1415 GMT), after touching its lowest level since September 2025 at $3,693.13 earlier in the session.

US gold futures for December delivery fell 0.8% to $3,711.50 per ounce.

"Interest rate expectations and a strong dollar are two factors weighing on gold prices today. Minutes from last month's FOMC meeting showed almost all Fed officials expected interest rates will need to move higher, and inflation data released since that meeting support further rate increases here in the US," said Chris Gaffney, head of World Markets at EverBank.

The dollar index this week reached its highest level since April 2, 2025, making greenback-priced commodities like gold more expensive for buyers holding other currencies.

Fed minutes released on Wednesday showed policymakers in October saw rising inflation risks that may warrant a stronger policy response.

The minutes reinforced sentiments already expressed by several policymakers throughout the week, including Governor Christopher Waller, who said the central bank may need to respond more aggressively to rising prices.

Fed Governor Michael Barr said he would likely support tighter monetary policy in an economy still facing inflation pressures.

Traders see a 91% chance of a 25-basis-point rate increase in December and a nearly 9% probability of a larger 50-basis-point hike, <FedWatch>.

Higher interest rates reduce the appeal of non-yielding bullion by raising its opportunity cost.

In the near-term, markets would need to see increased demand for gold from both consumers and central banks for prices to recover from the one-year low, Gaffney said, adding, "the recent computer outages, and worries about AI could lead investors to turn back toward 'hard assets' such as gold."

Spot silver rose 0.6% to $45.28 per ounce, platinum gained 0.7% to $1,380.30, and palladium fell 1.4% to $934.86.

data.title: SentinelOne and Singapore Digital and Intelligence Service Team Up to Strengthen Cyber Defence and Advance Secure AI
data.description:
SentinelOne® (), the AI Security leader, today announced it will partner with the Defence Cyber Command (DCCOM) of the Digital and Intelligence (DIS) to collaboratively strengthen cyber defence and advance secure AI across Singapore’s defence and critical infrastructure sectors. The relationship was formalised at CIDEX 2026.

The rapid adoption of AI has fundamentally changed cybersecurity norms and best practices. In the few months alone, the emergence and exploitation of novel vulnerabilities, rogue AI agent behavior, and LLM-related supply chain attacks, have ushered in a new era in cyber governance and defence.

SentinelOne and DCCOM will explore bringing together the AI-native Singularity™ Platform, SentinelLABS™ AI and threat intelligence research, and training with DCCOM’s own expertise to help defenders evolve their practices and strategies to meet this new reality. As a result, human defenders can benefit from AI-powered security to detect, investigate, and respond to novel threats at machine speed.

Security That Fits Defence Environments

Defence networks need protection that does not depend on a cloud connection. The Singularity Platform supports on-premise and air-gapped deployment, so DCCOM can apply AI-native protection in environments where a cloud connection is not an option. For defenders, that means detection and response that stay inside the network boundary.

Four Areas of Cooperation

The parties will explore partnering in four areas:

- Cybersecurity technology and solutions

- Cyber threat intelligence sharing

- Research and innovation

- Training and capacity building

“Singapore is putting AI at the centre of how it defends itself and runs its critical systems, and the security behind that has to keep pace,” said Andrew Howell, VP, Government Affairs at SentinelOne. “This collaboration allows us to explore ways our platform, our research, and our training can be combined alongside DCCOM's own teams, so defenders can stop attacks at machine speed, including in air-gapped environments, and so more of the people doing that work are trained in Singapore.”

“Our MOU with SentinelOne will facilitate joint collaboration on AI-enabled technologies for cyber operations, for faster threat detection, investigation and response at machine speed,” said Brigadier-General Clarence Cai, Commander DCCOM/Defence Cyber Chief.

About SentinelOne

SentinelOne () is the leader in AI security, setting the standard for using AI and automation to give defenders a decisive operating advantage. Built for those who secure our world, its platform delivers unified coverage across endpoints, identity, cloud, and AI. Powered by Autonomous Security Intelligence, SentinelOne stops attacks at machine speed, reducing risk and delivering clarity and control to stay one step ahead. Headquartered in Mountain View, California, with teams worldwide, SentinelOne protects nearly one-fifth of the Fortune 500 and hundreds of Global 2000 enterprises. From Main Street to Wall Street, the world's most critical organizations trust SentinelOne with their security.

data.title: Bath & Body Works Dips on Q3 Results
data.description:
Bath & Body Works, Inc. today reported third-quarter 2026 results.

The company reported net sales of $1,577 million for the quarter ended October 31, 2026, a decrease of 1.0% compared to net sales of $1,594 million for the quarter ended November 1, 2025.

Earnings per diluted share were $0.19 for the third quarter of 2026 compared to $0.37 last year. Third-quarter operating income was $108 million compared to $161 million last year, and net income was $38 million compared to $77 million last year.

CEO Daniel Heaf commented, “Our third-quarter results exceeded our sales and adjusted earnings per share guidance, and marks encouraging progress in our Consumer First Formula. One year after introducing this strategy, we are seeing our actions translate into results across product, brand, and marketplace.”

“Our product innovation is resonating with customers and digital delivered its second consecutive quarter of growth. Our wholesale business with Ulta and Amazon continues to gain momentum and we are telling bigger and bolder brand stories through a more coordinated approach to marketing. While these are encouraging early proof points, we have more work to do to drive consistent growth across our channels.”

BBWI shares lost 10 cents to $18.56.

data.title: Why Micron, Intel and other AI stocks are getting a lift on Thursday
data.description:
By Hannah Pedone

Anthropic's IPO is one big reason - but there's also optimism about Texas's data-center landscape and a new buyback program from optical company Coherent

Micron's stock was up 6% on Thursday morning.

The Anthropic initial public offering is just one factor giving artificial-intelligence stocks a much-awaited boost on Thursday.

Shares of Coherent (COHR) were up 10% in morning trading. Shares of Lumentum Holdings (LITE), Micron Technology (MU), Marvell Technology (MRVL), Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) and Nvidia (NVDA) were up between 4% and 6%.

Anthropic's IPO is "pivotal" for the AI investment cycle, D.A. Davidson analyst Gil Luria told MarketWatch. Shares start trading later today, and the company on Wednesday disclosed that it upsized the deal and priced it above its target range.

The company is a direct and indirect customer for chip makers, and the IPO has already been seen by investors as a bellwether for the AI trade.

Luria said that a successful IPO could "extend the cycle by years," while an unsuccessful one could "stall investment" into the ecosystem.

That said, it remains to be seen whether the Anthropic excitement can drive a more sustained rally for AI stocks, which have been pressured recently amid concerns about financing and Nvidia's leadership shakeup.

Morningstar analyst Martin Szumski doubts the IPO will "fully turn around what has been very bearish sentiment lately." One reason is that investors saw Anthropic's prospectus weeks ago and "know relatively what to expect."

He believes most of the "uplift" in the AI world on Thursday relates to Anthropic excitement, but he also noted Wednesday's announcement that Texas has resumed issuing permits for data centers after pausing them last month.

Texas is a key state in the data-center buildout, though there is still "some question whether this willingness to approve new proposals that are not currently under construction will continue," he said.

There are some other company-specific drivers of stock excitement on Thursday, including Coherent's announcement of a new buyback program, a CoreWeave executive's disclosure that he had purchased some company bonds and reports of Intel's remarks from a conference indicating that the company locked in an outside customer for its 18A manufacturing technology.

CoreWeave's stock (CRWV) stock is up 7% in morning trading, while Intel shares (INTC) are up 7%.

-Hannah Pedone

data.title: Anthropic IPO Lifts Mood in Markets — WSJ
data.description:
By Rebecca Feng

The tech-heavy Nasdaq composite jumped nearly 2% on expectations of a pop in Anthropic trading, after the Claude maker pulled off a record-breaking initial public offering.

The S&P 500 also climbed more than 1%, setting up a day of gains after five consecutive down sessions.

Ahead of their public debut on the Nasdaq Thursday, Anthropic's shares traded as much as 25% above their IPO price of $83 a share in the gray market. That price was set above the company's target range of $70 to $78 a share.

Investors view Anthropic's IPO as a major test for the artificial intelligence trade. Strong demand for the AI giant's shares helped ease recent fears surrounding the AI bubble and temporarily diverted investors' attention away from the dramatic departure of Jensen Huang from Nvidia.

Frank Downing, director of research at ARK Investment Management, which has been an investor in Anthropic since 2023, said on CNBC Thursday that the company's IPO is a huge milestone, but still "very early" in what will be a spectacular run for these software and AI companies.

Write to Rebecca Feng at rebecca.feng@wsj.com

This item is part of a Wall Street Journal live coverage event. The full stream can be found by searching P/WSJL (WSJ Live Coverage).

data.title: Countries weigh banning smart glasses over privacy concerns
data.description:
Governments, courts and companies are considering restrictions and reviewing existing rules on smart glasses amid worries that the technology, popularized by Meta's Ray-Bans, could be used to photograph, film or audio-record confidential materials or people without their knowledge.

Here is a summary of what countries and regions are doing to protect people's privacy, in alphabetical order.

AUSTRALIA

The federal government said in September it was considering barring the use of camera-equipped smart glasses in government workplaces due to privacy and security concerns.

Public Service Minister Katy Gallagher asked the country's Public Service Commission for advice on whether their use should be prohibited and what exemptions might be required.

BRITAIN

Courts in England and Wales have prohibited the use of Meta smart glasses because of restrictions on taking images and videos in courts.

British cinema operators are also introducing policies to prohibit ​or restrict camera-enabled smart glasses, the UK Cinema Association said in August.

EUROPEAN UNION

Smart glasses have attracted scrutiny from European privacy regulators and some lawmakers, and the European Data Protection Board has commissioned a report into their "social acceptability".

Member of the European Parliament Veronika Cifrová Ostrihoňová also urged the European Commission, which has not proposed legislation specifically targeting smart glasses, to consider possible action.

NETHERLANDS

The Netherlands' privacy watchdog AP has advised consumers to not buy smart glasses, saying they are unsafe for both users and bystanders, after studying six types available in the Dutch market.

The agency, which cannot independently impose a blanket ban on smart glasses, said concerns with such devices extend beyond privacy to include safety risks and software vulnerabilities.

NORWAY

The government said it planned to propose a temporary ban on the use of ​AI glasses in places where the public ​regularly gather, such as parks, beaches, museums, shopping centres and public events.

Norway's capital Oslo banned smart glasses in schools in August.

UNITED STATES

New York's Unified Court System banned smart glasses from all its court facilities from July 20. The rule covers prescription and non-prescription eyewear or headwear containing cameras, microphones, computers or other technology capable of recording video or audio. Visitors carrying them must hand them over to court personnel for safekeeping before entering.

data.title: US natural gas stockpiles likely rose by 27 billion cubic feet last week
data.description:
US energy firms likely added an above-normal 27 billion cubic feet of natural gas into storage last week, according to the average estimate in a Reuters poll released on Wednesday.

Some 6 bcf were withdrawn during the same week a year ago. Over the past five years, the average increase for that week was 15 bcf (2021 to 2025).

In the prior week ended November 6, energy firms added 61 bcf of gas into storage. (USOILN=ECI)

If correct, the forecast for the week ended November 13 would increase stockpiles to 3.889 trillion cubic feet. That would be about 1.5% below the same week a year ago and about 2.3% above the five-year average for the week.

The US Energy Information Administration is scheduled to release its weekly storage report at 10:30 a.m. EST (1530 GMT) on Thursday.

There were 94 total degree days (TDDs) last week, lower than the 30-year normal of 112 TDDs for the period, data from financial firm LSEG showed.

Total degree days measure the number of degrees a day's average temperature is above or below 65 degrees Fahrenheit (18 degrees Celsius) to estimate demand to cool or heat homes and businesses.

Reuters polled 12 analysts, whose estimates ranged from injections of 10 bcf to 38 bcf, with a median increase of 27 bcf.

Early estimates for the week ending November 20 showed an average decrease of 4 bcf.

That figure compares with a withdrawal of 11 bcf during the same week last year and a five-year average decrease of 24 bcf.

data.title: Schools in UK, Nigeria, Pakistan among winners in global prizes
data.description:
Schools in Britain, Nigeria, Brazil, Pakistan and South Korea were named winners of the World's Best School Prizes on Thursday for work including supporting student well-being, helping under-served communities and coordinating support for children with complex learning needs.

The winners are invited to January's World Schools Summit in London to present their approaches to policymakers and education figures, organiser T4 Education, a global network for educators, said.

The annual prize comes weeks after high school pupils in France blockaded schools demanding renovation of their buildings, more teachers and university reforms — a movement that broadened into protests over the cost of living, drawing in trade unionists and activists and at times turning violent.

"Young people are simply worried about their future," T4 Education and prizes founder Vikas Pota told Reuters. "What our schools are doing ... especially the winning schools ... (is that) they're all giving students hope for a better future... They're responding to what the communities want."

Swiss Cottage School, Development and Research Centre, a London state primary and secondary special school, won the Community Collaboration prize for bringing together different services to support pupils with complex learning needs, many from lower-income backgrounds. The school links education, community participation, therapy, healthcare and employability support, connecting classroom learning to the wider world.

Slum2School Green Academy in Epe, Nigeria, won the Environmental Action prize. The charity-run kindergarten and primary school, which serves about 250 children from river communities, was recognised for its environmentally designed buildings and a model combining practical, project- and play-based learning.

The school runs on solar power and is built from natural materials such as wood and bamboo. Pupils learn about sustainable practices including water conservation, waste management and renewable energy.

Public primary school Escola Municipal GET IV Centenario won the Overcoming Adversity prize for its hands-on learning model focused on creativity, emotional development and student leadership, serving 261 students. Based in Rio de Janeiro's Complexo da Maré favela community, the school was closed for 37 days in 2024 because of local violence. It runs a "Dream Factory" program in which pupils use technology to address local problems.

The Supporting Healthy Lives award went to TNS Beaconhouse, an independent school in Lahore with more than 1,100 students across kindergarten, primary and secondary levels, for its approach to supporting neurodivergent learners.

Independent secondary school G-School in Seoul won the Innovation prize. Each of its nearly 70 students takes on a long-term social problem-solving project; one team persuaded 27 local businesses to install wheelchair ramps to improve accessibility.

A separate prize decided by public vote, the Community Choice award, went to Darussafaka Egitim Kurumlari, a full-scholarship boarding school in Istanbul, for a two-track model that includes remote learning for children affected by earthquakes.

data.title: Volkswagen demands pay freeze, flexible hours in looming showdown with union
data.description:
Volkswagen laid out its demands on Thursday for upcoming wage talks, including freezing salaries for the next two years, setting the stage for a showdown with unions that could culminate in strikes at the turn of the year.

In a bid to slash production costs, the embattled automaker also wants to eliminate a bonus paid out either in cash or as paid leave, and get an option to increase working hours if needed without raising salaries.

The IG Metall union, for its part, is demanding a 5% pay rise.

Relations between management and the union, which has significant influence over company strategy under Volkswagen's corporate structure, have been tested by CEO Oliver Blume's ramped-up restructuring drive, with 100,000 job cuts planned.

Workers have threatened to strike from January after Volkswagen terminated almost all of its wage deals with the union.

Volkswagen and IG Metall begin wage negotiations on Tuesday in the northwestern town of Emden, home to one of four plants that the group could close from early next decade under the restructuring.

data.title: France's Fiscal Arithmetic Remains Worrying — Market Talk
data.description: Despite recent analysis suggesting that France's economic woes are overblown, its public finances remain under significant pressure, Andrew Kenningham at Oxford Economics says in a note. "If our forecasts are accurate, France would need to run a broadly balanced primary budget by 2030 if its debt is to be on a stable trajectory at that point," Kenningham says. With a deficit of around 3% of GDP expected this year, an adjustment of 3% of GDP will be required by 2030. This is unlikely without significant external pressure, for example from the bond market, he says. An improvement in global markets, a rebound in French GDP or reassuring plans from the next government could ease concerns. "But the arithmetic itself is definitely worrying." (don.forbes@wsj.com)

data.title: Chile's environmental regulator files charges against Codelco copper mine
data.description:
Chile's environmental regulator SMA has filed charges against state-run miner Codelco's Ministro Hales copper mine over alleged failures to comply with measures aimed at controlling particulate matter emissions in the northern city of Calama, it said on Thursday.

  • Charges follow inspections and seven citizen complaints filed between 2021 and 2024 in Calama, SMA said

  • One charge relates to the operation of the mine's primary crusher without the bag-filter system required under its environmental permits, it added

  • A second charge alleges the mine failed to apply bischofite, a dust-suppression treatment, in inactive sections of its waste dump in 2023 and 2024, and lacked records showing implementation of the measure between 2023 and 2025

  • Both infractions were classified as serious and could result in the revocation of the mine's environmental permit, temporary closure of the operation, or fines of up to $4.3 million each, the regulator said

  • The Ministro Hales mine produced 146,000 tons of copper in 2025, according to Codelco figures

  • Codelco is one of the world's largest copper producers; the charges were first reported by newspaper La Tercera

data.title: Airtel ranked as India’s Most Valuable Brand : Kantar BrandZ India 2026
data.description:
Airtel emerged as India’s most valuable brand at a valuation of $43.2 billion, up 5 per cent over last year, as per the latest edition of Kantar BrandZ rankings. HDFC, Tata Consultancy Services, State Bank of India and ICICI Bank were ranked among the top five most valuable brands. However, India’s Kantar BrandZ Top 100 Most Valuable Brands ranking estimated the combined brand valuation at $460.3 billion, witnessing a decline of 12 per cent year-on-year.

The report noted that Airtel has been focusing on consistent investments in strengthening brand equity and evolution from a connectivity provider into a broader digital ecosystem enabling it to grab the top spot.

Meanwhile, e-commerce marketplace Meesho (No.59) is 2026’s Top Riser, boosting its brand value 64 per cent to $1.9 billion. Its affordable, mobile-first proposition makes online shopping accessible to more consumers, with orders growing 45 per cent in FY26, the statement added.

Also, Blinkit emerged as the highest new entrant($4.3 billion), successfully extending quick commerce beyond grocery into a wider everyday retail repertoire, it noted.

On the 12 per cent decline in combined brand valuation, the report noted that this comes at a time when brands are managing the pressures of moving towards AI-enabled transformation. Deepender Rana, Kantar’s Executive Managing Director, South Asia, said, “India’s economy is still expanding, and both mass and premium brands have room to grow here. With global crises stoking inflation, consumers continue to face stresses that impact their everyday decisions.

In this environment, brands need to chart a course that confidently balances short-term pressures with long-term brand building. This requires the right intelligence, and the ability to connect this intelligence to action.” He noted that India also has less exposure to the AI-led technology and media categories driving brand value growth in other parts of the globe.​

data.title: Sandisk's stock split is almost here. This is what investors need to know.
data.description:
By Hannah Pedone

Sandisk is conducting an 8-for-1 stock split after a sharp surge in its share price

Sandisk will undergo an 8-for-1 stock split.

Sandisk is due to split its stock after Thursday's close, and while the move has gotten some buzz, it won't alter the fundamental picture for shareholders of the memory-chip company.

The company (SNDK) announced the 8-for-1 stock split in October, noting that the stock price had "increased significantly" since the company spun off from Western Digital (WDC) in February 2025. When completed, shareholders will own eight shares for each share they owned before.

The company says the move will make the stock "more accessible" to investors, a common refrain among management teams when they announce splits. The logic is that higher stock prices might turn investors away, though experts note that the rise of fractional trading lessens that concern.

Sandisk's stock closed Wednesday at $776.

Steve Sosnick, chief strategist at Interactive Brokers, told MarketWatch that it's not unusual for companies to split their stocks after such big moves. The decision, while announced in late October, could have been planned prior to that, he said, given that the stock was "coming off its extraordinary highs."

Sandisk designs and manufactures "non-volatile" NAND flash memory, which can save data without needing a constant source of power. The memory is used in phones, data centers and other hardware, for which there has been growing demand in the AI era.

Shares of Sandisk have run up 1,495% since the February 2025 spinoff, according to Dow Jones Market Data. But at their highest point earlier this summer, they were up 4,704% since the time of the separation.

"Maybe they felt that this would add some appeal to the stock as it was starting to dip," Sosnick said of Sandisk's management team.

Sosnick explained that while a stock split can improve liquidity for options traders, it doesn't change the true value for ordinary investors.

Options contracts typically represent 100 shares of stock per contract, he explained. Therefore, a lower share price following a split can make options contracts more accessible to investors with less cash.

Yet he said that while the split has "some side benefits for options traders," that's "not the company's motivation."

Rather, its goal is to "ratify the perception that the company has done well enough to justify a stock split," and also to offer the perception that shares are more affordable.

John Dunfee, CEO of JD Group Holdings, told MarketWatch that a split can drive more retail investors toward the stock, but it's "never an investment thesis."

Investors should avoid thinking that the price after the split is cheaper than the price before, he noted: "It's the same company." What matters more is the company's earnings potential over the next year or two, according to Dunfee.

"The real money is made by understanding earnings before the market does, not by counting shares."

Once the split is complete, "excitement settles" and "fundamentals and earnings take over," he added. "They always do," he said.

-Hannah Pedone
